articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft patches 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously-named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. Because nothing says 'secure by design' like triple-digit patch counts.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian GRU hackers are mass-harvesting Microsoft Office tokens by exploiting old router vulnerabilities. Your home router is basically a free ATM for state-sponsored spies at this point.

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Utah's new anti-VPN law goes live, because apparently the First Amendment doesn't apply to digital privacy. Watch VPN usage skyrocket faster than a Mormon missionary fleeing coffee shops.

articles.title: Digital Hopes, Real Power: From Connection to Collective Action
articles.summary: States are scrambling to block public records about ALPR surveillance after FOIA requests exposed their sprawling spy networks. Democracy dies in darkness, but surveillance thrives there too.

articles.title: Democratic Leaders Wanted to Control the Maine Senate Race. Their Pick Just Dropped Out.
articles.summary: Senator Ron Wyden is making NSA bootlickers cry, and Tom Cotton is threatening 'consequences' for asking uncomfortable questions. Because nothing screams 'freedom' like intimidating elected officials.

articles.title: PyTorch Lightning and Intercom-client Hit in Supply Chain Attacks to Steal Credentials
articles.summary: A 15-year-old allegedly pwned France's secure document agency for 18 million records. When teenagers are your biggest national security threat, maybe reconsider your cybersecurity strategy.

articles.title: Linux cryptographic code flaw offers fast route to root
articles.summary: New 'Copy Fail' Linux vulnerability (CVE-2026-31431) gives unprivileged users root access across major distros. Even the penguin isn't safe from catastrophically dumb coding mistakes.

articles.title: Editorial. Challenge of Mythos
articles.summary: Microsoft's patch for a Russian-exploited zero-day was so bad they had to patch the patch. CISA warns attackers are still having a field day with Windows systems.

articles.title: Sri Lanka discloses another missing payment, days after hackers stole $2.5M from its finance ministry | TechCrunch
articles.summary: DPRK hackers are using AI to inject malware into npm packages, because North Korea apparently has better DevOps than most Fortune 500 companies. Claude Opus unwittingly became an accomplice.

articles.title: Wiz finds AI has moved from tool to infrastructure, broadening the attack surface
articles.summary: US-Estonian suspect Peter Stokes arrested in Finland for alleged Scattered Spider ties. The international manhunt continues as authorities slowly piece together the cybercrime syndicate's web.
